1.explanation: The heart of the issue is in the ListBoxMenuItem component: it unconditionally sets tabIndex="-1" on every option container, so none of the items is ever included in the Tab order. Downshift’s getItemProps provides the role="option" (and event handlers) but never overrides tabIndex, so all option elements remain non-focusable. To fix the violation, ListBoxMenuItem (or the Dropdown’s getItemProps call) must implement a roving tabindex pattern—setting tabIndex="0" on the highlighted (or active) option and "-1" on the others—so that at least one option is tabbable when the listbox is open.
1.bug_scenario: When the Carbon Dropdown is opened (either in the storybook canvas or on the demo site), the underlying <div role="option"> elements rendered for each menu item are all marked with tabIndex="-1" (via the ListBoxMenuItem component). Because none of the option-role elements is actually focusable by Tab, the IBM Equal Access Checker raises a “None of the descendant elements with 'option' role is tabbable” violation.

2.explanation: The Dropdown component uses a ListBoxMenuItem for each option. In ListBoxMenuItem.js you can see that every rendered option container has tabIndex="-1" unconditionally. Downshift’s getItemProps injects role="option" but because the element is not in the tab sequence (tabIndex = -1), the accessibility checker flags that no option is tabbable. To fix this, ListBoxMenuItem should set a focusable tabIndex (e.g. 0 when highlighted or active) or honor the tabIndex provided by getItemProps instead of hard-coding "-1".
2.bug_scenario: When the user opens a Dropdown and inspects it with the IBM Equal Access Accessibility Checker, the tool reports a critical violation: “None of the descendent elements with ‘option’ role is tabbable.” In the DOM snapshot you can see that the open menu is rendered with a parent role="listbox" and each option is rendered as a div with role="option" (via Downshift) but has tabIndex="-1" hard-coded. Because tabIndex is -1, these option elements can’t be reached by keyboard focus, causing the accessibility violation.
